raw.assessment: The incumbent preserved every ordered design and caught seven fitting defects before dispatch. Rework affected five of eight large covers and two of fourteen medium covers, making size-dependent fit a useful lead, not an established cause. Unadjusted small covers met the time target, but neither other sizes nor the batch median are thereby validated. The concrete limiting observation is H2-O3: reference tables omit rounded corners found on both observed installation failures, so reference fit cannot establish customer fit. Estimated waste by weight does not establish the contractual area limit.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create systematic size-dependent fit errors; cloth behavior and execution remain competing explanations.
openings.delta: Make the existing cutting card testable before committing the whole stock, using a staged start with ordered covers.
openings.prediction: An allowance problem predicts repeatable signed fit deviations by size despite accurate cutting and sewing. Deviations tracking operator, cutting direction or cloth behavior instead weaken that account.
openings.probe: For an initial cover of each size, record order, cut and sewn dimensions, design, direction, operator, signed reference-fit error and stage times. Compare any repeated size errors across workers before changing allowances. Measure offcut length and width through the stipulated wash test. Confirm revised covers survive five cycles; calculate the complete cutting layout by area before adoption.
assumptions: Initial covers remain usable ordered stock.
Any revision must demonstrate no more than 8% cutting waste, cost at most 350, and readiness within three weeks.

openings.claim: Do customer fitting failures follow corner geometry when actual tabletop dimensions agree with the order, or follow dimensional discrepancies regardless of corner shape?
openings.delta: Distinguish two reasons a cover can pass the reference check yet require installation adjustment.
openings.prediction: Failure concentrated at rounded corners with matching dimensions supports a corner-pocket hypothesis; failure on square tables with dimension discrepancies supports order-measurement mismatch.
openings.probe: Request actual dimensions and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where available. Compare first-placement fit of their ordered covers with reference-table fit, recording where adjustment occurs. Seek contrasting geometry and dimension combinations; if unavailable, retain the ambiguity.
assumptions: Measurements clarify specified tables without substituting ordered sizes or designs.
Any subsequent pocket revision still requires wash, removal, waste, cost and timing verification.

raw.assessment: The stipulated observations locate rework mainly in larger covers and identify a possible customer-table geometry mismatch. They do not establish causes or show that removing rework alone achieves the 32-minute median. Preserve ordered sizes, designs, purchased stock, wash durability and removable installation.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: sewing and checking an initial cover of each size before releasing the remaining cuts could prevent repeated fit errors caused by the common allowance.
openings.delta: Replace whole-batch cutting with a small calibration stage; change a size allowance only when measurements support it.
openings.prediction: If allowance mismatch contributes, initial medium or large covers will show repeatable dimensional shortfall at the reference table, and subsequent corrected covers will require fewer seam reopenings. Irregular errors would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Record intended dimensions, actual cut dimensions, sewn dimensions and separate cutting/sewing/fitting times on the initial three covers. Measure retained offcuts in both directions before and after the stipulated wash sequence. Check any allowance revision against a full-batch cutting layout measured by area before further cutting; include calibration work in batch time accounting and verify wash performance.
assumptions: Any revision retains the ordered visible design and table size.
A feasible layout stays within 8% area waste; changes remain within 350 currency units and three weeks.
Initial covers remain usable batch items.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry explain customer placement failures after actual tabletop dimensions are accounted for?
openings.delta: Distinguish a corner-pocket compatibility problem from inaccurate nominal dimensions using a separate observable fit comparison.
openings.prediction: A geometry explanation predicts failures concentrated at rounded corners despite agreement in actual length and width; a dimension explanation predicts mismatch across corner types when actual and nominal dimensions differ.
openings.probe: Request actual length, width, thickness and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing the four nominal-only orders if reachable. Compare these with orders and reference tables. Before releasing affected cuts, observe first placement of an initial cover on a measured customer table; record whether interference occurs at corners or across straight spans. Any proposed pocket revision must separately pass wash, removal, time and area-yield checks.
assumptions: The willing customers include relevant table geometries and can provide reliable measurements.
Actual measurements clarify the specified table without substituting an ordered size or design.
Customer access and any adjustment fit the existing deadline and budget.

openings.claim: Staged calibration may prevent repeated errors from a common allowance.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable signed size errors, including shortfall, support allowance mismatch; operator, design, direction or cloth associations support rivals. Corrections should reduce seam reopenings.
openings.fit: Preserves conditionally; initial covers must remain usable ordered items.
openings.probe: Before batch cutting, sew one per size; record intended, cut and sewn dimensions, signed fit errors, design, direction, operator and stage times. Compare repeated errors across workers before revision. Measure offcut shrinkage in both directions through five cycles; verify revised covers and full-batch layout by area. Include calibration time.
openings.uncertainty: Size association is not causation; small-cover times do not establish other sizes or batch median.

openings.claim: Customer geometry or dimensional discrepancies may explain failures despite reference fit.
openings.discriminator: Rounded-corner failures with matching dimensions support pocket incompatibility; discrepancies across corner types support measurement mismatch.
openings.fit: Preserves conditionally; measurements clarify specified tables without substituting orders.
openings.probe: Obtain length, width, thickness and corner measurements from six willing customers; prioritize nominal-only orders if reachable. Seek contrasting geometry/dimension combinations. Before affected cuts, compare ordered-cover first placement on measured customer and reference tables; locate corner versus straight-span interference.
openings.uncertainty: Measurement reliability, access and contrasting cases are unproven; retain ambiguity if unavailable.

lineage.reason: With A1; preserves rivals and signed errors.
With Z1; preserves staged release and time accounting.
With A2; preserves contrasting cases and ambiguity.
With Z2; preserves thickness and pre-cut placement.

post_distill.decision: Probe both; no cause established. Any revision must honor sizes/designs, purchased stock, five-cycle durability, tool-free removal, two machines, 350 budget, three weeks and <=8% area waste; weight estimate is insufficient. Verify >=95% first placement, all designs and <=32-minute median on 40 covers. Evidence is stipulated synthetic.
